The buy function always uses the setPrices function to set the sellPrice and buyPrice, but the setPrices function is not called, causing the buy function to always use the default price.
The sell function has an integer overflow where the amount is calculated as `msg.value / sellPrice`, but the sellPrice is never set, causing the function to always use the default sellPrice.

The mintToken function uses the random.seed function to set the balance of the owner, but the random.seed function is not a reliable source of randomness, causing the function to potentially produce arbitrary values.
The setPrices function is public, allowing any user to set the prices. This can be exploited. However, the contract owner should have the exclusive right to set the prices.
